question: The marked price of an article is ₹450. It is sold for ₹267.30, after offering three successive discounts of 10%, x%, and 20%. What is the value of x?
solution:
Given:

Marked price(MP) of an article is ₹450

Selling price of the article is ₹267.30

Discount %(D) = 10%, x%, and 20%

Concept used:

Selling price(SP) = MP × (100 - D)%

Calculation:

According to question,

Case(1) D = 10%

SP = 450 × (100 - 10)%

⇒ ₹405

Case(2) D = 20%

New SP = 405 × (100 - 20)%

⇒ ₹324

Case(3) D = x%

Final SP = 324 × (100 - x)%

⇒ ₹267.30 = 324 × (100 - x)%

⇒ 5670 = 324x

⇒ x = 17.5

∴ Required value of x is 17.5.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

In the 1st discount, 10 unit becomes 9 unit.

In the 3rd discount, 5 unit becomes 4 unit.

Let's assume, in the 2nd discount a unit becomes b unit

now,

⇒ (a)/(b) = (9×4times 450)/(10times 5times 267.3) = (40)/(33)

So, 40 becomes 33 after the 2nd discount

 

So, the value of x = (7)/(40) times 100 = 17.5
